title: SNAP work requirements and participation barriers
discussion_signal: The post frames work requirements as an access and administrative-burden issue, emphasizing paperwork, unstable work, school, internships, and food security. Replies add frontline concerns about households losing support while trying to build employment and education pathways.
linked_research_question: When benefit conditions are intended to raise employment, do they instead reduce participation and usable stability for people facing administrative or labor-market barriers?
limits: The post is advocacy and does not reproduce the five-state study's methods
Replies are not representative beneficiary opinion
Policy criticism does not by itself establish the size of employment effects
